fatal_errors: The proposed FCC CoCrFeMnNi alloy is not the dual-phase FCC/B2 Al0.7CoCrFeNi eutectic alloy in the target.
Computational composition optimization and conventional casting do not reconstruct the required 6 GPa, 1473 K, 2-hour HPHT treatment.
The hypothesis omits the transformation from incoherent lamellae to a hierarchical microstructure with coherent interfaces.
The proposed grain-refinement and twinning mechanism misses preferential FCC-to-B2 dislocation transfer, stress-concentration relief, and homogeneous strain partitioning.
The quantitative strength and ductility predictions are inconsistent with the reported approximately 1150 MPa strength and 36% elongation and have no cited support.
explanation: The response addresses the general strength-ductility problem in high-entropy alloys and proposes comparative tensile and microscopy tests, but it does not identify the material, HPHT method, processing window, structural transformation, or principal interface-mediated mechanism of the target. Its FCC stability boundary and arbitrary falsification thresholds do not discriminate the pressure-induced hierarchical-interface mechanism from ordinary casting effects. With no supporting evidence and quantitative claims disconnected from the target, it is unsupported rather than a reconstruction.
